Spyhound looks for traces of known spyware (for example Pegasus or Predator) and stalkerware on your phone – using published indicators from Amnesty International, Citizen Lab, MVT, and ECHAP.
This is not real-time antivirus. It only finds known traces. Nothing found does not mean you are safe. If you are genuinely worried, get help – for example from Access Now.
Checks stay on your device. No account, no telemetry. The app uses the internet only when you load updated indicator lists.
Basic runs right away. Set up the deep check once in the app – no PC, no root, no extra app. Root adds the strongest checks if your phone allows it.
Spyhound searches your phone for traces of known spyware and stalkerware, matched against published trace lists from research groups, Amnesty International (MVT), and the Echap association.
It is not live protection. It only knows published traces. A clear result covers the areas checked – not every risk. Seek expert help if you fear targeted surveillance.

Basic: apps, device settings, optional SMS and files. Deep: also processes and system logs – through wireless debugging on the phone itself (or Shizuku). Root: the same data with full access when available.
Scans stay offline. No usage statistics, no ads. Updates only fetch fixed files from allowed sources and check each one for changes.
Toolkit-curated lists (CC0) from the Zero Breach Toolkit are merged into the bundled sets. Amnesty and Citizen Lab feeds have no redistribution licence and load on the device only.
The malware list contains fingerprints of known Android malware from loaded sources. Only exact fingerprint matches count. Not a virus scanner, no replacement for Play Protect.

Spyhound is a private, non-commercial open-source project. No advertising, no paid features. Voluntary support via GitHub Sponsors does not unlock any features.

Controller: Belkis Aslani, Vogelsangstraße 32, 71691 Freiberg am Neckar, Germany (email below).

All check data – installed apps and their permissions, device settings, SMS links, files, system logs, bug reports – is processed only on your device. The controller does not receive it. No accounts, no telemetry, no analytics, no advertising, no sharing with third parties. Results, DNS hits and the “Who can do what” history stay local until you uninstall the app or clear its data. The app reads device information only as far as the check you start requires (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG). No automated decision under Art. 22 GDPR.

Network connections: if you trigger a list update (indicators, tracker and phishing domains), the app loads pinned files over HTTPS from raw.githubusercontent.com (GitHub, Inc., USA / GitHub B.V., Netherlands; Microsoft group). GitHub receives your IP address and standard HTTP data. Legal basis: Art. 6(1)(b), alternatively (f) GDPR. USA transfer: GitHub states that it is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Art. 45 GDPR). The scan and the background check use no network.

DNS guard (optional): a local VPN on the device that checks DNS queries against the lists and forwards them unchanged to your network's DNS server; “Block” answers them locally. Only if Android reports no DNS server, 9.9.9.9 (Quad9) or 2606:4700:4700::1111 (Cloudflare) is used. Only hits are stored, locally.

Built-in check service (optional): connects to the same device through wireless debugging over 127.0.0.1 only. Turn wireless debugging off after the check.

Permissions: installed apps, SMS (optional), all files (optional), internet (list update, DNS guard, connecting to this phone itself for the deep check without a PC), network state and VPN (DNS guard), notifications (pairing code, background finding, DNS guard), vibration, keep awake and start after reboot (background check only). Optional ones can be revoked at any time. Links open the browser only when you tap them.

“Share report” hands the text to Android's share menu only when you ask for it. You decide the recipient.

Your rights: access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection (Art. 15–21 GDPR) – contact the email below. Complaints: Der Landesbeauftragte für den Datenschutz und die Informationsfreiheit Baden-Württemberg, Heilbronner Straße 35, 70191 Stuttgart.

Spyhound only detects published traces of known spyware and stalkerware. No result is a guarantee: “no known traces in the areas checked” does not mean “safe”, and a finding can be a false positive. This is not legal, forensic or security advice. If you suspect targeted surveillance, contact the specialists listed under Help.

An app on your phone matches a trace that researchers found in government-grade spyware. This is serious, but not proof. False matches are rare, but possible.

1. Do not reset your phone or delete anything until an expert has looked at it. Otherwise evidence is lost.\n2. Contact the Access Now Digital Security Helpline (free): help@accessnow.org.\n3. Have private conversations from another device for now.
An app on your phone matches a known monitoring app. Such apps can send messages, location and photos to another person. A false match is possible.

1. Do not remove the app right away: the person watching you may notice. Get help first, for example from a local helpline for domestic abuse.\n2. Have private conversations from another device that nobody else can access.\n3. Once you are safe: open “App info” and tap “Uninstall”.

1. Do not open the link (again). Do not reset your phone or delete anything until an expert has looked at it. Otherwise evidence is lost.\n2. Contact the Access Now Digital Security Helpline (free): help@accessnow.org.\n3. Have private conversations from another device for now.

The fingerprint (SHA-256) of an app or file on your phone exactly matches a sample that security researchers (ESET, Meta) published as known malware. Such apps can spy on you, steal logins or take over banking. A match of this kind is exact, but the list only covers a few named campaigns.

1. Uninstall the app: Settings > “Apps” > the app > “Uninstall”. If it cannot be removed, first turn off device admin and accessibility access for it. Delete a file you downloaded yourself.
2. Change the passwords of your important accounts (email, bank, messengers) from another device, and turn on two-factor sign-in.
3. If you used banking or payment apps while it was installed, contact your bank.
4. Scan again afterwards. If you fear targeted surveillance, contact a specialist helpline.
The malware list contains fingerprints of known Android malware from loaded sources. Only exact fingerprint matches count. Not a virus scanner, no replacement for Play Protect.
1. You do not need to do anything.\n2. Keep Play Protect on and install apps from trusted stores only.
This app did not come from an app store and has far-reaching permissions. It is only a hint, not a finding: many harmless apps are installed this way.

1. Do you recognise the app and did you install it yourself? Then all is well.\n2. If not, open “App info” and check what it is allowed to do.\n3. Do not need it? Uninstall it. If you feel watched, get help first: removing it can be noticed.
This app can read your screen or resist being removed. Trusted apps such as password managers need this too. It is a hint, not a finding.
1. Open “Accessibility” in Settings and see which apps are switched on.\n2. Switch off what you do not know or need.\n3. If an app cannot be switched off or uninstalled, get help.
Your phone has not had a security update for a long time. This is not a finding, but spyware likes to use known flaws.
1. Look for system updates in Settings and install them.\n2. If there are none, the maker has dropped support. Plan for a newer phone.
A developer feature is on that lets a computer reach your phone without unlocking it. This is not a finding and is normal for developers.
1. If you did not switch it on yourself, open “Developer options” and turn off “USB debugging” and “Wireless debugging”.\n2. Always lock your phone with a PIN and keep it with you.
The start-up protection of your phone is loosened (unlocked bootloader). Tech fans often do this themselves. It is a hint, not a finding.
1. If you set this up yourself, all is well.\n2. If not, think about who had the phone before and ask an expert for advice.\n3. If you do not trust a second-hand phone, have it set up again.
Your phone runs a test version of Android that is less protected. It is a hint, not a finding.
1. If you installed a self-built or developer version, all is well.\n2. If not, ask an expert or reinstall the maker\'s system version.
A protection inside your phone\'s system (SELinux) is weakened. This happens with self-built systems or root. It is a hint, not a finding.
1. If you set this up yourself, all is well.\n2. If not, ask an expert for advice before you reset the phone.
Your phone shows traces of root, which is full control over the system. Tech fans often set this up themselves. It is a hint, not a finding.
1. If you set up root yourself, all is well.\n2. If not, ask an expert for advice before you reset the phone.
These apps may install other apps outside the app store. Browsers and file managers often need this. It is a hint, not a finding.
1. Open the setting and see which apps are allowed.\n2. Take the permission away from every app that does not need it.
The bug report is quite old. It cannot show traces that reached the phone later.
1. Create a new bug report and scan it.\n2. Also scan your phone directly in Spyhound.
This is a hint, not a finding. It may be harmless, but it is worth a look.
1. Read the description of the hint.\n2. If you understand what it means and it fits you, there is nothing to do. Otherwise ask an expert for advice.
Messages were not checked because Spyhound is not allowed to read them. This is neither a good nor a bad result, just a gap.
1. Allow Spyhound to read SMS. The messages stay on your phone.\n2. Scan again afterwards.
Files in storage were not checked because access to all files is missing. This is a gap, not a result.
1. Allow Spyhound to access files. Nothing is uploaded.\n2. Scan again afterwards.
One part of your phone cannot be checked without extra help. This is a gap, not a result.
1. Set up the deeper check. The guide leads you step by step.\n2. Scan again afterwards.
The innermost part of your phone was not checked because it needs root. This is a gap, not a result.
1. You do not need to do anything. The deeper check already covers a lot.\n2. If you strongly suspect something, ask an expert who can examine the phone more closely.
Spyhound does not know all traces yet because some lists are missing or damaged. It may therefore find less.
1. Connect to the internet and reload the lists.\n2. Scan again afterwards.
Some app files could not be read and so were not compared. This is a gap, not a result.
1. You do not need to do anything.\n2. Scan again later if you like.
For some apps the signature could not be read. They could not be compared with known traces.
1. You do not need to do anything.\n2. Scan again later if you like.
This part was empty or only partly readable and so was not fully checked. This is not a good result, just a gap.
1. Scan again, ideally with a charged battery and no other apps running.\n2. Set up the deeper check if you have not yet.
The bug report is missing a part or is incomplete. That part was not checked.
1. Create a new, complete bug report.\n2. Also scan your phone directly in Spyhound.
Very large files were not compared. This is a gap, not a result.
1. You do not need to do anything.\n2. Check large files you do not recognise by hand.
One check could not run completely. This is neither a good nor a bad result, just a gap.
1. Read the description of the gap.\n2. Scan again later.
